text.paragraph: New patient visit for chest tightness and breathlessness on exertion in a heavy smoker planning a polar expedition: risk assessment, ECG and blood tests, starting treatment, smoking and alcohol counseling, and a cardiology referral. Concerns: He is afraid a heart diagnosis will stop the expedition he has promised to lead; He will be weeks from a hospital at sea and in the far south. [S]

list.item: Polar explorer and expedition leader; organizing a ship-based scientific expedition to the Antarctic and sub-Antarctic islands that sails from London in about four months, with a long sea passage and weeks out of reach of a hospital [S]
Married; lives in London while he organizes the expedition, working long days on finance, the ship, stores, and the crew [S]
Tobacco: about 25 cigarettes a day since 16 (about 39 pack-years); has never tried to stop; first cigarette within 30 minutes of waking [S]
Alcohol: three or four drinks on most evenings at dinners with backers, more at weekends (AUDIT 12, hazardous range); no withdrawal symptoms; no other drugs [S]
Exercise: none regular since his last expedition; heavy lifting of stores at the dock; walks fast [S]
Does not want anything recorded or done that could stop the expedition; uneasy about being examined, and agreed after his reasons were heard [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for chest tightness and breathlessness on exertion in a heavy smoker planning a polar expedition: risk assessment, ECG and blood tests, starting treatment, smoking and alcohol counseling, and a cardiology referral
Two-week follow-up and cardiology consultation with coronary CT angiography and echocardiogram
Six-week review: angina on medical therapy, smoking, and a shared decision about coronary angiography and stenting
Ten-week review: three weeks after the stent, lipids, cardiac rehabilitation, smoking and alcohol
Four-month review before departure: exercise test, lipids, HbA1c, and the expedition medical plan
Same-day sick visit for low back pain

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Cardiology consultation in two weeks with coronary CT angiography for suspected stable angina, and advice on revascularization and on fitness for the expedition

Medical therapy from intake for suspected angina: aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 80 mg, metoprolol succinate, and sublingual nitroglycerin with written instructions to call emergency services if pain lasts more than 5 minutes after the first dose
Stop smoking: varenicline for 12 weeks, with the option of 12 more, a quit date in one week, counseling at each visit, and the quitline
AUDIT with a brief intervention for hazardous drinking: no more than two drinks a day and several alcohol-free days a week, with AUDIT-C at follow-up
Prediabetes: diet and activity counseling and HbA1c in about four months

Raise metoprolol succinate to 100 mg for persisting angina, with an echocardiogram, and revascularization of the proximal LAD lesion if angina persists despite medical therapy or he prefers it after a shared decision

Expedition plan: a symptom-limited exercise test before departure, a written cardiac summary with ECG and stent card, three months' extra medicines split between two bags, an automated external defibrillator and emergency cardiac medicines on board, a satellite link for telemedicine, an evacuation plan to the nearest cardiac centers along the route, and advice on cold stress
Invasive coronary angiography with a drug-eluting stent to the proximal LAD, then aspirin with clopidogrel for six months and aspirin alone after
Cardiac rehabilitation after the stent, three sessions a week until departure, with a home exercise plan for the voyage
Add ezetimibe 10 mg because LDL cholesterol was 62 mg/dL on atorvastatin 80 mg, above the target below 55
No cigarettes from the quit date, confirmed at each visit
Not smoked since the quit date a week after intake; varenicline continued to 24 weeks
LDL cholesterol below 55 mg/dL with at least a 50% reduction by four months
Blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg by six weeks
Free of angina in daily activity, and a symptom-limited exercise test of at least 10 METs without ischemia before departure
No angina since the stent; about 12.8 METs without angina or ST changes
Drinking within the low-risk limit, with an AUDIT-C below 4, by four months
AUDIT-C 3, from an AUDIT of 12; two drinks at most on four evenings a week
At least 15 sessions of cardiac rehabilitation before departure
